ul.li: If yes, shred it. No further action is required.

ul.li: If yes, go to Fraud indicators are present . Fraud indicators are present

In FTS, determine if the banking information has been changed to the banking information on the potentially fraudulent application:

ul.li: If no, go to Fraud indicators are present . Fraud indicators are present

In NWS, create a new SROC as follows:

ul.li: Details: Type “[Type of undeliverable mail] initially sent on [date] was received as undeliverable on [date] — new address on file.”

step.cmd: In PSCD, determine if the client’s new address is available as follows:

ul.li:
On the Debtor Overview - BP search screen, do the following:
Social Insurance Number: Enter the client’s SIN.
Select Search .
If the client’s new address is not available, go to step 9. If the client’s new address is available, go to step 10.

step.cmd: Determine if a new address for the client is available from a third-party source (e.g. directory assistance or the telephone book).

ul.li: If no, fact-find with the client to obtain a new address. Go to step 11. fact-find

step.cmd: Fact-find with the client to verify the address from the third-party source. Go to step 11.
Determine if the client was contacted during fact-finding:

ul.li: If yes, refer to Change of address and go to step 12. Change of address
If no, go to New address unconfirmed or unknown . New address unconfirmed or unknown

step.cmd: In NWS, add details to the draft SROC created during fact-finding or create a new SROC as follows:

ul.li: Details: Type “[Type of undeliverable mail] initially sent on [date] was received as undeliverable on [date] — client stated the new address is [new address].”
Go to New address confirmed . New address confirmed
